criteria.criterion: States that 'down' is not proof the host is dead
criteria.evidence: "Nova marks a compute service down when its heartbeat stops... The QEMU guests may still be running and still writing to their Ceph RBD images."

criteria.criterion: Explains the risk of two running copies writing to the same storage
criteria.evidence: "Evacuation starts 40 new guests on other hosts against the same RBD images. Ceph won't stop a second writer by default... silent corruption"

criteria.criterion: Requires fencing via out-of-band management or switch isolation before evacuation
criteria.evidence: Evacuation is allowed only "If the host is confirmed dead (powered off through BMC, not just unreachable)", followed by "Make sure it stays powered off" and a Ceph blocklist of the old watchers. It does not mention switch isolation and does not say what to do when the host is unreachable but its power state is unknown.

criteria.criterion: Proposes read-only checks before any action
criteria.evidence: "Check first (read-only, a few minutes)": BMC/IPMI power state, ping/SSH, virsh list, external reachability of the VMs, rbd status watchers, and a check for non-Ceph storage.

criteria.criterion: Considers business criticality / ordering of evacuations
criteria.evidence: "Evacuate in batches, databases first". It gives a basic priority order but no input from the customers or business owners about criticality.

"Confirm each VM reaches ACTIVE with its volumes attached", "check its crash-recovery log and run its integrity check", and keep cmp-0417 off. It does not check that the VMs are reachable on the network or that no instance is left on the old host.

criteria.criterion: Names who must authorize the evacuation
criteria.evidence: The response never says who decides or approves the evacuation.

critical_errors.error: approves evacuating before the host is confirmed powered off or isolated
critical_errors.evidence: Evacuation is gated on "confirmed dead (powered off through BMC, not just unreachable)".

critical_errors.error: treats Ceph shared storage as making evacuation safe without fencing
critical_errors.evidence: It explicitly warns that "Ceph won't stop a second writer by default".

critical_errors.error: recommends automation that evacuates on lost heartbeat without fencing
claims instances have been or will be recovered without evidence
critical_errors.evidence: "I haven't seen your environment and haven't run any of these commands."

summary: This is a strong, safe answer. It says clearly that 'down' does not prove the host is dead, explains the split-brain risk of two copies writing to the same Ceph images, gives read-only checks first, and allows evacuation only after the host is confirmed powered off through the BMC, with a Ceph blocklist added for safety. It has three gaps. It never names who must authorize the evacuation. Its priority order is just databases first, with no input from the customers. Its post-evacuation checks leave out network reachability and a check that no instance remains on the old host. It commits none of the critical errors and has no faithfulness issues.
